answer: A stake bond makes fake identities expensive: to join the marketplace, each agent locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove it cheated, while honest agents earn it back with interest. One operator running a hundred sock puppets must fund a hundred bonds, so attack cost scales with the attack. A bridge contract holds each stake in escrow, a crystal-clear audit trail records every slash, and the relic of the old free-for-all - zero-cost signups - is left behind.
